On-Chain Operator. Module 7 · On-chain analytics. Navy and cyan. This is the door, not the whole module. Education only.
You can already read a token's supply and a protocol's fees. Analytics is how you check those claims on the ledger itself.
By the end of the module you will be able to do this: read on-chain data without over-interpreting it. Not before. The lessons earn it one page at a time.

The lessons, in order, are 7.0 Mastery Starter, 7.1 On-chain data foundations, 7.2 Block explorer mastery, 7.3 Exchange flows, 7.4 Whale & entity analysis, 7.5 Holder & supply metrics, 7.6 Network activity, 7.7 DEX & liquidity analytics, 7.8 Derivatives on-chain, 7.9 Querying chain data yourself. You do not skip ahead. Each page is the input to the next.
Lesson 7.0, Mastery Starter. Mastery Starter. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.1, On-chain data foundations. Avoid the classic misreads of on-chain data. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.2, Block explorer mastery. Read any transaction on an explorer without using the app's interface. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.3, Exchange flows. Interpret exchange inflows and outflows with the right caveats. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.4, Whale & entity analysis. Use large-holder data without copying wallets blindly. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.5, Holder & supply metrics. Read MVRV, SOPR and HODL waves as context, not signals. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.6, Network activity. Judge a chain's real usage beyond transaction counts. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.7, DEX & liquidity analytics. Measure whether a pool can actually absorb your trade and pay you as an LP. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.8, Derivatives on-chain. Read funding, open interest and liquidation data as positioning context. You will write that down when you get there.
Lesson 7.9, Querying chain data yourself. Answer your own research questions with on-chain queries, instead of relying on someone else's dashboard. You will write that down when you get there.
